title: Length: Centimetres and Metres
seo_title: Grade 3 Length Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Length: estimate, measure, compare, order and record length using standard units (metres and centimetres); solve problems involving length.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 3 maths worksheets: measuring length in centimetres and metres, reading rulers and length stories. 100 questions with pictures and memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Use centimetres (cm) for short lengths and metres (m) for long lengths.
  • 100 cm = 1 m.
  • Start measuring at 0 on the ruler.
  • To compare lengths, use the same unit.

Examples

Example

1 m and 45 cm

100 cm + 45 cm

Answer: 145 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Starting at 1Start at 0.
The wrong unitA pencil is cm, a field is m.
Mixed unitsChange m to cm first.

faq.a: Grade R to Grade 3 in South African schools. Grade 3 is the last year; learners are about 8 to 9 years old.

faq.q: Which units of length are in Grade 3?

faq.a: A ruler, a metre stick or a tape measure.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the height of the classroom door?
items.e: A door is a bit taller than an adult, about 2 m. Litres measure how much a container holds.

items.q: How many metres are in 1 kilometre?
items.e: Kilo means 1 000. So 1 km = 1 000 m.

items.q: Which list goes from the shortest unit to the longest unit?
items.e: A millimetre is the smallest. 10 mm make 1 cm, 100 cm make 1 m, and 1 000 m make 1 km.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A classroom door is about ☐ tall.
items.e: A door is a bit taller than an adult. That is about 2 m. 2 cm is shorter than your finger.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A new pencil is about ☐ long.
items.e: A new pencil fits on a 30 cm ruler, so it is about 19 cm. 19 mm is only about as long as a fingertip.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A Grade 3 learner is about ☐ tall.
items.e: Most Grade 3 learners are between 1 m and 1 m 50 cm tall. 130 cm fits. 13 cm is the size of a hand.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A school bus is about ☐ long.
items.e: A school bus is about as long as 6 classroom doors lying end to end, so about 12 m.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. You can walk about ☐ in 15 minutes.
items.e: A 15-minute walk is a good benchmark for 1 km. You can walk 1 m in one big step.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the length of the school swimming pool?
items.e: A pool is long, but you can walk along it in a minute, so use metres. Litres measure capacity, not length.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the mass of a watermelon?
items.e: A watermelon is heavy, so use kilograms. Litres measure how much a container holds.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the mass of a strawberry?
items.e: A strawberry is very light, so use grams.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure how much water a bathtub holds?
items.e: A bathtub holds a lot of water, so use litres.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure how much medicine fits on a spoon?
items.e: A spoon holds only a little, so use millilitres.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the mass of a school backpack?
items.e: A full backpack is quite heavy, so use kilograms.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the length of a cricket pitch?
items.e: A cricket pitch is about 20 m long. You can walk along it in a short time, so use metres.

items.q: Which unit measures mass?
items.e: Mass is how heavy something is. We measure mass in grams and kilograms. Kilometres sound like kilograms, but they measure length.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A large carton of milk holds about ☐.
items.e: Big milk cartons from the supermarket hold 2 ℓ. 2 mℓ is less than half a teaspoon.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A whole watermelon has a mass of about ☐.
items.e: A whole watermelon is heavy to carry, about 6 kg. 6 g is as light as six paper clips, and 60 kg is as heavy as a grown-up.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A paper clip has a mass of about ☐.
items.e: A paper clip is very light. 1 g is about the mass of one paper clip.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A teaspoon holds about ☐.
items.e: A teaspoon holds only a little, about 5 mℓ. 5 ℓ would half fill a bucket.
The pencil starts at 0 and ends at 7. So it is 7 cm long. Count the spaces between the numbers, not the marks: there are 8 marks but only 7 spaces.
The crayon starts at 0 and ends at 5. So it is 5 cm long. Count the spaces between the numbers, not the marks: there are 6 marks but only 5 spaces.
The rubber starts at 0 and ends at 4. So it is 4 cm long. Count the spaces between the numbers, not the marks: there are 5 marks but only 4 spaces.
The piece of ribbon starts at 0 and ends at 9. So it is 9 cm long. Count the spaces between the numbers, not the marks: there are 10 marks but only 9 spaces.
The pencil starts at 2, not at 0. It ends at 9. 9 − 2 = 7, so it is 7 cm long. You can also count the spaces from 2 to 9: there are 7.
The crayon starts at 1, not at 0. It ends at 6. 6 − 1 = 5, so it is 5 cm long. You can also count the spaces from 1 to 6: there are 5.
The rubber starts at 3, not at 0. It ends at 7. 7 − 3 = 4, so it is 4 cm long. You can also count the spaces from 3 to 7: there are 4.
The piece of ribbon starts at 2, not at 0. It ends at 8. 8 − 2 = 6, so it is 6 cm long. You can also count the spaces from 2 to 8: there are 6.
The pencil starts at 3, not at 0. It ends at 11. 11 − 3 = 8, so it is 8 cm long. You can also count the spaces from 3 to 11: there are 8.

items.q: Ravi puts one end of his crayon at 1 on the ruler, not at 0. The other end is at 8. How long is it?
items.e: He started at 1, so the number at the end is 1 too big. 8 − 1 = 7 cm.

items.q: Anika puts one end of her library card at 1 on the ruler, not at 0. The other end is at 10. How long is it?
items.e: She started at 1, so the number at the end is 1 too big. 10 − 1 = 9 cm.
The crayon goes past 4 cm and then 6 small marks more. 4 cm = 40 mm, and 40 + 6 = 46. So it is 46 mm long.
The pencil goes past 6 cm and then 3 small marks more. 6 cm = 60 mm, and 60 + 3 = 63. So it is 63 mm long.
The rubber goes past 3 cm and then 5 small marks more. 3 cm = 30 mm, and 30 + 5 = 35. So it is 35 mm long.
The pencil starts at 2 cm, not at 0. It ends at 7 cm and 4 small marks, which is 74 mm. 2 cm = 20 mm. 74 − 20 = 54 mm.
The crayon starts at 3 cm = 30 mm. It ends at 8 cm and 8 small marks, which is 88 mm. 88 − 30 = 58 mm.

items.q: Megan measures a ribbon. It goes from 0 to 6 on the ruler. She counts the marks 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and says the ribbon is 7 cm. How long is it really?
items.e: Megan counted 7 marks, but length is the number of spaces between them. From 0 to 6 there are 6 spaces, so the ribbon is 6 cm.

items.q: Each small square is 1 cm on each side. What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: Count the 1 cm sides all the way around: 4 + 2 + 4 + 2 = 12 cm. 8 is the number of squares inside. That is the area, not the perimeter.

items.q: Each small square is 1 cm on each side. What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: Count the 1 cm sides all the way around: 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16 cm. 15 is the number of squares inside. That is the area, not the perimeter.

items.q: Each small square is 1 cm on each side. What is the perimeter of the square?
items.e: Count the 1 cm sides all the way around: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12 cm. 9 is the number of squares inside. That is the area, not the perimeter.
The pencil starts at 0 and ends at 7. So it is 7 cm long. Count the big spaces, not the numbers.
The crayon starts at 0 and ends at 5. So it is 5 cm long. Count the big spaces, not the numbers.
The rubber starts at 0 and ends at 4. So it is 4 cm long. Count the big spaces, not the numbers.
The piece of ribbon starts at 0 and ends at 8. So it is 8 cm long. Count the big spaces, not the numbers.
The rubber starts at 3, not at 0. It ends at 7. 7 − 3 = 4, so it is 4 cm long. You can also count the big spaces: there are 4.
The crayon goes past 4 cm and then 6 small marks more. Each small mark is 1 mm. So it is 4 cm 6 mm long.
The pencil goes past 6 cm and then 3 small marks more. Each small mark is 1 mm. So it is 6 cm 3 mm long.
The rubber goes past 3 cm and then 8 small marks more. Each small mark is 1 mm. So it is 3 cm 8 mm long.
The rubber is 3 cm and 5 mm long. 3 cm = 30 mm, and 30 + 5 = 35. So it is 35 mm long.
The pencil starts at 2 cm, not at 0. It ends at 7 cm 4 mm. Take away 2 cm: 7 cm 4 mm − 2 cm = 5 cm 4 mm.
The crayon starts at 3 cm, not at 0. It ends at 7 cm 8 mm. Take away 3 cm: 7 cm 8 mm − 3 cm = 4 cm 8 mm.

items.q: Daniel has 85 cm of ribbon. He cuts off 30 cm. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: Cutting off means subtract: 85 − 30 = 55 cm.

items.q: Mpho has two pieces of ribbon. One is 45 cm long. The other is 38 cm long. How much ribbon is there altogether?
items.e: Add: 45 + 38. 5 + 8 = 13, so exchange 10 ones for 1 ten. 45 + 38 = 83 cm.

items.q: A sunflower was 35 cm tall. It grew 18 cm more. How tall is it now?
items.e: Add: 35 + 18 = 53 cm. Remember to exchange: 5 + 8 = 13.

items.q: Elna builds a train track 3 m long. She adds 1 m 50 cm more track. How long is the track now?
items.e: Add the metres: 3 m + 1 m = 4 m. Then add the 50 cm. The track is 4 m 50 cm long.

items.q: Ravi has 1 m 40 cm of string. He ties on 80 cm more. How long is the string now?
items.e: 40 cm + 80 cm = 120 cm = 1 m 20 cm. Add this to 1 m: 1 m + 1 m 20 cm = 2 m 20 cm.

items.q: Thabo needs ribbon to wrap presents. He has 2 m of ribbon and uses 75 cm. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: 2 m = 200 cm. Subtract: 200 − 75 = 125 cm. 125 cm = 1 m 25 cm.

items.q: On sports day, Priya jumps 1 m 85 cm. Palesa jumps 2 m 10 cm. How much further does Palesa jump?
items.e: 1 m 85 cm = 185 cm and 2 m 10 cm = 210 cm. Count on: 185 → 200 is 15 cm, 200 → 210 is 10 cm. 15 + 10 = 25 cm.

items.q: A brown worm is 45 mm long. A pink worm is 6 cm long. Which worm is longer, and by how much?
items.e: 6 cm = 60 mm. 60 mm is more than 45 mm, so the pink worm is longer. 60 − 45 = 15 mm. Do not take 6 from 45: change to the same unit first.

items.q: Fatima has 85 cm of ribbon. She cuts off 30 cm. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: Cutting off means subtract: 85 − 30 = 55 cm.

items.q: Find the missing number. 1 m 5 cm = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Add the 5 cm: 100 + 5 = 105 cm. It is not 15 cm, and it is not 150 cm.

items.q: Find the missing number. 1 m 50 cm = ☐ cm
Find the missing number. 2 m 30 cm = ☐ cm
Find the missing number. 4 cm 5 mm = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm, so 4 cm = 40 mm. Add the 5 mm: 40 + 5 = 45 mm.

items.q: Find the missing number. 1 kg 200 g = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1 000 g. Add the 200 g: 1 000 + 200 = 1 200 g. 300 g would mean 1 kg = 100 g.

items.q: Find the missing number. 1 kg 50 g = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1 000 g. Add the 50 g: 1 000 + 50 = 1 050 g. The 5 is in the tens place.

items.q: Find the missing number. 1 ℓ 500 mℓ = ☐ mℓ
items.e: 1 ℓ = 1 000 mℓ. Add the 500 mℓ: 1 000 + 500 = 1 500 mℓ. 600 mℓ would mean 1 ℓ = 100 mℓ.

items.q: Which is the same as 320 cm?
items.e: 100 cm = 1 m, so 300 cm = 3 m. 320 cm = 3 m and 20 cm left over.

items.q: Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Change them all to grams: 1 kg = 1 000 g, 1 kg 50 g = 1 050 g. So the answer is 1 kg 50 g.

items.q: Which is the lightest?
items.e: Change them all to grams: 1 kg = 1 000 g, 1 kg 20 g = 1 020 g. So the answer is 600 g.

items.q: Which holds the most?
items.e: Change them all to millilitres: 1 ℓ = 1 000 mℓ, 1 ℓ 200 mℓ = 1 200 mℓ. So the answer is 1 ℓ 200 mℓ.

items.q: Which holds the least?
items.e: Change them all to millilitres: 2 ℓ = 2 000 mℓ, 1 ℓ 900 mℓ = 1 900 mℓ, 2 ℓ 50 mℓ = 2 050 mℓ. So the answer is 1 ℓ 900 mℓ.

items.q: Each small square is 1 cm on each side. What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: Count the 1 cm sides all the way around: 6 + 2 + 6 + 2 = 16 cm. 12 is the number of squares inside. That is the area, not the perimeter.

items.q: Each small square is 1 cm on each side. What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: Count the 1 cm sides all the way around: 2 + 5 + 2 + 5 = 14 cm. 10 is the number of squares inside. That is the area, not the perimeter.

items.q: Each small square is 1 cm on each side. What is the perimeter of the shape?
items.e: Go around the outside and count every 1 cm side, including the short step: 18 cm. There are 14 squares inside, but that is the area.

items.q: What is the perimeter of this triangle?
items.e: Add every side: 11 + 12 + 14 = 37 cm. Touch each side as you add it so you do not skip one.

items.q: What is the perimeter of this triangle?
items.e: Add every side: 11 + 8 + 11 = 30 m. Touch each side as you add it so you do not skip one.

items.q: What is the perimeter of this quadrilateral?
items.e: Add every side: 5 + 5 + 6 + 5 = 21 cm. Touch each side as you add it so you do not skip one.

items.q: What is the perimeter of this quadrilateral?
items.e: Add every side: 6 + 6 + 7 + 6 = 25 m. Touch each side as you add it so you do not skip one.

items.q: What is the perimeter of this pentagon?
items.e: Add every side: 5 + 6 + 5 + 8 + 4 = 28 cm. Touch each side as you add it so you do not skip one.

items.q: Priya’s family has a vegetable garden that is 8 m long and 5 m wide. They want a fence all the way around it. How much fence do they need?
items.e: The fence goes around all 4 sides: 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26 m. 40 is the area, and 13 m is only two sides.

items.q: One lap around that field is 500 m. How many laps make 1 km?
items.e: 1 km = 1 000 m. 500 m + 500 m = 1 000 m, so 2 laps make 1 km.

items.q: Sarah glues ribbon around the edge of a square picture frame. Each side is 25 cm. How much ribbon does she need?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides: 25 + 25 + 25 + 25 = 100 cm. 75 cm forgets one side.

items.q: The class bulletin board is 120 cm long and 90 cm wide. Mr. Singh puts a paper border around it. How long is the border?
items.e: Add all 4 sides: 120 + 90 + 120 + 90 = 420 cm. 210 cm is only one length and one width.

items.q: A park is shaped like a triangle. Its sides are 120 m, 150 m and 90 m. Sibusiso walks once around the park. How far does he walk?
items.e: Add the 3 sides: 120 + 150 + 90 = 360 m.

items.q: A dog pen is 9 m long and 4 m wide. One long side is the wall of the house, so it needs no fence. How much fence is needed for the other 3 sides?
items.e: Only 3 sides get fence: 4 + 9 + 4 = 17 m. 26 m would put fence along the house wall too.

items.q: Ethan’s family paddles their canoe 3 km to an island and 3 km back to the cottage. How far do they paddle?
items.e: There and back is 3 km + 3 km = 6 km.

items.q: Ethan used 30 m of fence to go around a rectangular garden. The garden is 9 m long. How wide is it?
items.e: Two lengths: 9 + 9 = 18 m. 30 − 18 = 12 m for the two widths. 12 ÷ 2 = 6 m.

items.q: A square sandpit has a perimeter of 12 m. How long is each side?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides. 12 ÷ 4 = 3 m. Check: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12.

items.q: Garden A is 8 m by 2 m. Garden B is 5 m by 5 m. Which garden needs more fence to go around it?
items.e: A: 8 + 2 + 8 + 2 = 20 m. B: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20 m. They need the same fence. B has more space inside (25 is its area), but the same perimeter.

items.q: A rug is 3 m long and 2 m wide. Lerato sews a strip of trim around all the edges. How much trim does she use?
items.e: Perimeter = 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 10 m. 6 is the area of the rug, and 5 m is only two sides.

items.q: Lerato wants to put tape around the edge of a table that is 90 cm long and 60 cm wide. She has 250 cm of tape. Is that enough?
items.e: Perimeter = 90 + 60 + 90 + 60 = 300 cm. 300 cm is more than 250 cm, so it is not enough. 150 cm is only one length and one width.

items.q: What is the perimeter of this triangle?
items.e: Add every side: 5 + 6 + 8 = 19 cm. Touch each side as you add it so you do not skip one.

items.q: What is the perimeter of this triangle?
items.e: Add every side: 11 + 3 + 11 = 25 m. Touch each side as you add it so you do not skip one.

items.q: What is the perimeter of this quadrilateral?
items.e: Add every side: 6 + 5 + 7 + 4 = 22 m. Touch each side as you add it so you do not skip one.

items.q: What is the perimeter of this pentagon?
items.e: Add every side: 7 + 7 + 7 + 10 + 5 = 36 cm. Touch each side as you add it so you do not skip one.

items.q: What is the perimeter of this pentagon?
items.e: Add every side: 7 + 7 + 6 + 12 + 6 = 38 m. Touch each side as you add it so you do not skip one.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 long sides and 2 short sides: 9 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 26 cm. Adding only 9 + 4 = 13 forgets the other two sides.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 long sides and 2 short sides: 12 + 5 + 12 + 5 = 34 m. Adding only 12 + 5 = 17 forgets the other two sides.

items.q: This is a square. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24 cm.
